sections.theory:
Movement of blood in the chambers of the heart

In both chambers on the right side of the heart impure blood (Deoxygenated Blood) is present, and in both chambers on the left side pure, i.e. oxygen-rich, blood (Oxygenated Blood) is present.

In the same way, between the right atrium and the right ventricle there is a valve (Valve), which is called the tricuspid (Tricuspid) valve. In the same way the middle valve (Valve) between the left atrium and the left ventricle is called the bicuspid valve (Bicuspid Valve).

Blood vessels

Aorta

This is the largest artery in the body and it arises from the left ventricle (Left ventricle) of the heart, and it supplies pure (Oxygenated Blood) blood full of nutrition to the whole body.

Superior vena cava and inferior vena cava

These two blood vessels bring impure blood (Deoxygenated Blood) from the upper and lower parts of the body into the right atrium (Right Atrium) of the heart.

Pulmonary Arteries

These two arteries, leaving the right ventricle of the heart, send impure blood (Deoxygenated Blood) to the lungs for cleaning.

Pulmonary Veins

These veins bring pure blood (Oxygenated Blood) from the lungs back into the left atrium of the heart, i.e. …

In the same way, between the right atrium and the right ventricle there is a valve (Valve), which is called the tricuspid (Tricuspid) valve. In the same way the middle valve (Valve) between the left atrium and the left ventricle is called the bicuspid valve (Bicuspid Valve).

Aorta

This is the largest artery in the body and it arises from the left ventricle (Left ventricle) of the heart, and it supplies pure (Oxygenated Blood) blood full of nutrition to the whole body.

These two blood vessels bring impure blood (Deoxygenated Blood) from the upper and lower parts of the body into the right atrium (Right Atrium) of the heart.

These two arteries, leaving the right ventricle of the heart, send impure blood (Deoxygenated Blood) to the lungs for cleaning.
